VERIFIED in a probe importing ONLY DivisorFamilyFieldSurj + DivSchemeAbel, no pic-c file, lake env lean EXIT=0. The correct claim is narrower and still worth having: trivZar is the first inhabitant at a GENERAL TEST RING R, where no field-surjectivity route applies.\n\nUNIQUENESS RE-DERIVES A LANDED LEMMA. presentationDivisor_eq_zero_of_isCertified_zero + divEq_of_isCertified_zero (:103, :114) work per-adaptation and then re-run divEq_of_presentationDivisor_eq. But divFamDivisor_injective (DivisorFamilyFieldEquiv.lean:177) is exactly that step already packaged at the QUOTIENT level, and DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroUnique.lean imports DivisorFamilyFieldEquiv directly. With zero_le_divFamDivisor (DivisorFamilyField.lean:165) and deg_divFamDivisor (DivisorFamilyFieldCRT.lean:376), both also in closure, the whole file's math is:\n  hx : divFamDivisor x = 0 := eq_zero_of_deg_le_zero K (zero_le_divFamDivisor x) (deg rewrite; norm_num)\n  same for y; exact divFamDivisor_injective (hx.trans hy.symm)\nVERIFIED at the file's exact import list minus DivisorFamilyDegreeZero, EXIT=0.       "body": "REPLACING A HAND-ROLLED HYPOTHESIS BY 'THE STANDARD ONE' CAN STRENGTHEN IT INTO FALSITY -- and the test is a REFUTATION probe at the intended object, not a satisfiability witness.\n\nMEASURED (pic-e, AJC 0095 r7). I built the vocabulary the project was missing (graded prime avoidance => FiniteInAffine for projective schemes, all sorry-free), then restated the seam's antecedent with IsProjective of the representing scheme in place of the elementary FiniteInAffine, and committed 'entirely in standard vocabulary, no condition invented in this project'. I ran THREE vacuity checks and all three PASSED: the new conjunct is satisfiable (Spec k is projective over itself), it is NOT free (exact? fails at an arbitrary object), and the new antecedent does not close hypothesis-free. A fresh-context audit then refuted it in one step.\n\nWHY THE CHECKS MISSED IT. Every one of them asks 'could this hypothesis hold SOMEWHERE?'. None asks 'does it hold AT THE OBJECT THE STATEMENT IS ABOUT?'. IsProjective over a field forces IsProper, hence UniversallyClosed, hence CompactSpace over the compact Spec k -- and Pic_{C/k} is a disjoint union over deg in Z, so it is not quasi-compact. The antecedent is FALSE at its only intended witness. Satisfiability elsewhere is exactly what makes that invisible.\n\nWORSE: my own project already had the refutation. Picard/AmbientPicNotProper.lean exists to record this as 'trap (c): a P -> Q whose antecedent is unsatisfiable in the intended setting', with the general theorems to check it -- and I had imported nothing from it. The strengthening was FROM a weak condition my own file proved holds at the curve TO one my own project proved fails at the Picard scheme.\n\nTHE GENERALISABLE RULE. When you replace a hypothesis H by a 'more standard' H', H' => H is not enough -- that direction is what makes the substitution LOOK conservative. Ask what H' implies that H does not (here: quasi-compactness), then check that consequence at the intended witness. And grep your own tree for a file whose title is a negation ('NotProper', 'NoGo', 'Refute') before publishing a strengthening: the counterexample is often already landed one import away.\n\nALSO: the weakened repair is where tautologies hide. My first repair -- 'every finite set that lies in a good open lies in an affine open' -- is PROVABLE for every scheme with its hypothesis unused. Elaborate the candidate weakening with the binder discarded before shipping it (pic-g filed the same shape as I-1660 the same day).",

      "body": "AN 'ONLY PRODUCER IS FIELD-ONLY' CLAIM IS A CENSUS OF THE NAME YOU GUESSED, AND THE RING-LEVEL VERSION IS OFTEN LANDED UNDER A DIFFERENT MAP.\n\nMEASURED (pic-g 0096 r6, refuted by a fresh-context audit of my own file). I published that the picEtAffineEquiv/unit presentation seam has exactly one general producer -- PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section -- that it is stated over a FIELD and needs a curve section there, and that ring-level surjectivity of PicEtAff.unit is therefore the honest next brick. Every clause was checkable and the conclusion was false: picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt (PicEtUnit.lean:161) supplies the same seam at an ARBITRARY test RING, no field, no section, no curve binder, with 11 call sites.\n\nWHY MY CENSUS MISSED IT, and this is the reusable part. I searched for producers of the SEAM'S NAME -- surjectivity of  -- because that is the shape of the conclusion I wanted. The landed producer is not about 's surjectivity at all: it is an AFFINE-CONSISTENCY lemma for a DIFFERENT map (relPicToPicEt) which happens to have the seam as its conclusion. A grep for 'unit_surjective' finds it never; a search for the CONCLUSION 'picEtAffineEquiv _ = PicEtAff.unit _ _' finds it first.\n\nSO THE RULE: when you are about to write 'the only producer is X, and X is too strong', search for the CONCLUSION you need, not for the strengthened statement whose name you have. The name census answers 'who proved this lemma'; the obligation is 'who lands this Prop', and a lemma about another map can land it while carrying none of the binders you were about to price.\n\nAND THE SECOND-ORDER COST, which is why this is worth a memory item rather than a header note: the false claim RELOCATED THE GAP. I named ring-level surjectivity of  as the next brick; the actually-open statement is surjectivity of relPicToPicEt onto picEt -- a different map, different proof, and one the tree already treats as a real condition (Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:199 calls membership in its range 'honesty'). A misidentified next brick sends the next lane to build something nobody needs.",

      "body": "A \"TRAP, MEASURED -- DO NOT ROUTE VIA X\" NOTE IS THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE FALSE CLAIM A LANE CAN SHIP, AND THE CHEAPEST TEST IS TO GREP WHETHER A SIBLING FILE ALREADY DOES X.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (AJCR, pic-c 0092 r5, Pic0VanishingFieldGenusZero.lean:33-38). A lane recorded, in a file header, a commit message, and a direct message to another lane: \"going through chi_moduleKSheaf at baseChangeBundle C K produces the same object under a different Over instance, and the two chi terms DO NOT UNIFY -- measured\". It reads like exactly the kind of hard-won spelling fact worth broadcasting, and the receiving lane accepted it.\n\nIt is false. The bundled route closes with one `change` to the bundled spelling followed by `simpa`, at DEFAULT heartbeats. What had been measured was that one `simpa` failed without the `change`, i.e. a fact about a tactic invocation, published as a fact about two objects.\n\nTHE TEST THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT COST ONE GREP. A sibling lane had written the prohibited proof, at a concrete curve, in the same hour, and it was at HEAD and root-imported: Curve/P1DegreeZeroTrivial.lean:83-99 uses chi_moduleKSheaf at baseChangeBundle with the same change + simpa. So before publishing \"route X does not work\", grep the tree for X: a live use site refutes the prohibition outright, and its presence in a file you did not write is more likely than it feels, because a prohibition is usually discovered exactly when two lanes are on the same object.\n\nWHY IT IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY OVERCLAIM. A positive overclaim gets tested when someone tries to use the result. A prohibition is never tested -- its whole function is to stop people trying -- so it can survive indefinitely and it forecloses a cheap route for every later round. Same asymmetry as [[gap-list-is-the-least-audited-prose]] and [[exculpatory-sentence-is-a-claim]], but with a longer half-life.\n\nCOROLLARY, same round, same file: unexplained `set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000` raises with a comment asserting the default is exceeded. Copying both files verbatim with the default budget: EXIT=0, all six declarations. A budget raise is a claim too, and re-running the file at the default is a 40-second check.",

      "body": "A --summary WRITE IS A SILENT DESTRUCTIVE EDIT, AND THE TOOL'S OWN OUTPUT CANNOT SHOW IT. Check the commit STAT, not the command's success line.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-c, AJCR 0092 r1). I claimed a row with roadmap set --owner --status --summary. The CLI printed 'Updated roadmap item' and nothing else. The commit stat then read 46 insertions / 117 DELETIONS. --summary REPLACES; the 117 lines were review-ajcr's rank-elevation analysis of that exact fork, TWO author self-retractions inside it, and the row's stated live target. I had read the row earlier in the session, but through roadmap list, which truncates -- so I never saw the body I was about to overwrite.\n\nWHY THE EXISTING LESSONS DO NOT COVER IT. The workspace has roadmap-yaml-edit-reverts-owner (a prose edit writing a stale OWNER over a live claim) and several items about staged deletions of other lanes' FILES. This is neither: the owner field was fine, no file was staged D, the write was to a row I legitimately hold, and the loss was entirely inside one YAML string. Every file-level check passes.\n\nTHE RULE, cheap and it is the only one that works. After any roadmap set --summary, read the commit stat. A deletion count above a handful means you replaced prose you never read. Recover with git show <commit>^:<path>, merge the prior summary verbatim, append yours behind a marker saying what happened, and re-verify a distinctive phrase from the old text is present.\n\nTHE SHARPER POINT. The destroyed text contained a retraction whose lesson was 'a probe with the hypothesis as a BINDER measures the conversion, so the control looks audited' -- i.e. I deleted a warning about exactly the class of error a reviewer had just caught me making elsewhere in the same session. Board prose is where a lane's corrections live, and it is the least protected thing in the workspace: no build breaks, no test fails, no file appears deleted.",

      "body": "Degree-zero pic0TypeFunctor is not yet Kleiman's identity component\n\nMeasured: Pic0Functor.lean:103-153 defines pic0TypeFunctor through fibrewise degree zero.       "body": "A THREE-LANE COMPOSITION IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY PER-ROW CHECK, AND THE ROWS WILL EACH TELL YOU THE WORK IS ELSEWHERE.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-e, AJC, 0095 r6). Three sorry-free theorems from three different lanes composed into a verbatim derivation of the project's central sorry from the classical pointed theorem: the unconditional finite-GALOIS-level rational point (Curve/), the picSharp->picEt transport (PicEtSubcanonical), and the lftFree descent step with hq and hcov already internal (PicEtGaloisQuotient). Eleven declarations, all axiom-clean, three commits.\n\nNO ROW MENTIONED THE OTHER TWO. The descent-assembly row listed FOUR open inputs; three were already discharged elsewhere. The seam docstring's own 'what remains' sentence listed three items, one of which was closed and one of which was DONE-AND-CALLED-REMAINING. Every row was individually plausible and internally consistent; the composition existed only across them.\n\nTHE MECHANISM, and why the usual checks miss it: each row is maintained by the lane that owns it, and a lane records what IT owes, not what another lane has since supplied. So a row goes stale in the CHEAP direction -- it schedules work that exists -- and nothing re-reads it, because a list of remaining obligations reads as self-criticism. Same asymmetry as [[gap-list-is-the-least-audited-prose]] and [[unavoidable-is-not-geometric]], but distributed: no single sentence is wrong enough to notice.\n\nTHE CHECK THAT FINDS IT, and it is cheap: take the consumer theorem's LITERAL binder list -- #check the one a costing tells you to aim at -- and ask of EACH binder, separately, 'does a producer for exactly this exist at HEAD?'. Not 'is this gap open' (the row answers that) but 'is this BINDER discharged'. At the spelling that matters, seamClauseOne_of_hasGaloisQuotient_lftFree, three of four were gone and the fourth was an instance binder no row named. A four-item gap list and a one-item binder list were both accurate about different things.\n\nCOROLLARY, the part that cost me a withdrawal: after composing, price the RESULT against the WEAKEST antecedent your proof consumes, not the shape the hand-off wants. My first antecedent carried IsSeparated, which is provably free from the conclusion's own representation, and a reduction whose antecedent contains a free conjunct misreports exactly the number it exists to report. Related: [[price-the-consumer-carrier]], [[audit-the-goals-antecedents-not-the-lemmas]].",

      "body": "A LOCALISATION REDUCTION IS EMPTIED BY THE CONSUMER OWN OUTER QUANTIFIER, AND EVERY PER-STATEMENT CHECK PASSES.\n\nMEASURED (pic-g, AJCR 0096 r7, Pic0RingZariskiLocal.lean; audit I-1657/I-1660, reproduced by me).\n\nWHAT HAPPENED. I reduced an obligation P(A) at an arbitrary test algebra to a pointwise-local form: for every prime p of A, some f outside p with P(Localization.Away f). At a FIXED A that is a real reduction with no route back, and I verified it. I then composed it over all A into two producers of the goal object -- and those hypotheses are LOGICALLY EQUIVALENT to the global ones they were meant to weaken, because Localization.Away f is ITSELF a test algebra, so the consumer own forall-A already ranges over it. The converse is one line with the trivial witness f = 1.\n\nWHY EVERY CHECK PASSED. Sorry-free, axiom-clean against a sorryAx control, rooted, build green, non-vacuous (both hypotheses used, linter clean), and the fixed-A lemma genuinely is a reduction. Nothing local to any statement is wrong. The defect is the INTERACTION between my inner quantifier and the consumer outer one, and no per-statement check can see it.\n\nTHE TEST, and it costs one probe: before pricing a localisation, pointwise, or restriction reduction as progress, PROVE THE CONVERSE WITH THE TRIVIAL WITNESS -- f = 1, the identity localisation, V = top, the whole space. If it closes, the reduction only helps at a FIXED base object, and you must then check whether the consumer has that shape. Mine did not.\n\nSECOND, SMALLER TRAP FROM THE SAME FILE: my \"local ring\" interface was about Localization.Away f, which is a BASIC OPEN and not a local ring (IsLocalRing fails to synthesize). A lane with a genuinely local computation holds Localization.AtPrime, and the AtPrime-to-Away bridge is spreading out -- ask which one your consumer actually has before naming the interface.\n\nSibling of \"substitute the trivial value in layer one\" and \"free factor vs localisation\".",

      "body": "VANISHING-VOCABULARY SPELLINGS ARE ONE ANTECEDENT -- and the commit that ships the 'reduced' producer often ships the iff that proves it is a re-spelling.\n\nAJC DivFamilyZero.lean, AJC.picrep.divzero, pic-e runs 0095->0105. Over three rounds the same lane landed three producers of Div0-representable, each 'reducing' the obligation to a fresh vocabulary:\n  _of_isZero               : IsZero x.F\n  _of_forall_subsingleton_sections : forall V, Subsingleton Gamma(x.F,V)\n  _of_forall_isEmpty_schematicSupport : IsEmpty(schematicSupport x.F)\nEach docstring bills its antecedent as 'the sharpest/purest/most-geometric honest form.' At every DivFamily x.F is quasicoherent, and the file itself ships isZero_iff_forall_subsingleton_sections and isZero_iff_isEmpty_schematicSupport -- so the three antecedents are PROVABLY EQUIVALENT (all = IsZero x.F). None is weaker. The obligation HasFiberDeg 0 -> IsZero x.F is untouched; only the vocabulary on its RHS rotates.\n\nTHE TELL, sharper than I-1622: when a 'reduction' commit also lands an IFF between the new antecedent and the old one, the iff IS the proof that no reduction happened. Emptiness-of-support, subsingleton-sections, and IsZero are one node with three names; a producer parameterised on any of them is the same producer. Before crediting 'reduced to X', rw the shipped iffs and check whether the new antecedent closes the old goal with no hypotheses -- if it does, it is coordinates, not distance. The real distance for divzero lives in DivSupportQuasiFinite.lean (carrier bridge + degree-0=>empty-fibre), which no spelling of the RHS moves.",

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0FiniteStageGlueDataAssembly
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0FiniteStageTransitionModels
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModels

/-!
# An inhabited finite-stage Picard glue package

The simultaneous pair- and triple-transition descent theorems supply every input of
`pic0FiniteStageAffineRingGlueData`.  This file records those dependent inputs in one
package and immediately exposes the resulting scheme glue datum.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory TensorProduct
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

noncomputable section

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [IsSepClosed k]

set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 400000 in
-- The fields retain three nested finite-subextension scalar towers.
set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
/-- All finite-stage models and comparison equations needed to assemble the descended
Picard atlas.  The fields are outputs of the simultaneous finite-subextension producers,
not additional geometric hypotheses. -/
structure Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    (F : Type u) [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k] where
  L : DatG0.FinSubext F k
  n : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C -> Nat
  m : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C -> Nat
  relation : forall j, Fin (m j) -> MvPolynomial (Fin (n j)) L.1
  e : forall j,
    k ⊗[L.1] DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1 (n j) (m j) (relation j) ≃ₐ[k]
      Pic0FiniteStageRing C j
  M : DatG0.FinSubext L.1 k
  mapM : forall q : Pic0FiniteStageMapIndex C,
    Pic0FiniteStageModelRing C L n m relation M
        (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q) →ₐ[M.1]
      Pic0FiniteStageModelRing C L n m relation M
        (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q)
  hmapM : forall q,
    (Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val
        (AlgHom.id L.1
          (DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1
            (n (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))
            (m (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))
            (relation (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))))).comp
        ((mapM q).restrictScalars L.1) =
      ((pic0FiniteStageTransportedMap C L n m relation e q).restrictScalars
        L.1).comp
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val
          (AlgHom.id L.1
            (DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1
              (n (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))
              (m (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))
              (relation (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q)))))
  hOpen : forall i : Pic0FiniteStageRestrictionIndex C,
    IsOpenImmersion
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (mapM (Sum.inl i)).toRingHom))
  N : DatG0.FinSubext M.1 k
  thetaN : forall p : Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionIndex C,
    N.1 ⊗[M.1] Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelSource
        C L n m relation M mapM p →ₐ[N.1]
      N.1 ⊗[M.1] Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelTarget
        C L n m relation M mapM p
  hthetaN : forall p : Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionIndex C,
    (Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val
        (AlgHom.id M.1
          (Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelTarget
            C L n m relation M mapM p))).comp
        ((thetaN p).restrictScalars M.1) =
      ((pic0FiniteStageTransportedTripleTransitionOfModels
        C L n m relation e M mapM hmapM p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2).restrictScalars
          M.1).comp
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val
          (AlgHom.id M.1
            (Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelSource
              C L n m relation M mapM p)))

namespace Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage

set_option maxHeartbeats 25600000 in
-- The package projections retain the dependent tensor-product instances of the constructor.
/-- The scheme glue datum computed from an inhabited finite-stage package. -/
noncomputable def glueData
    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) : Scheme.GlueData := by
  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.L.1 k := by infer_instance
  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.M.1 k := by infer_instance
  exact pic0FiniteStageAffineRingGlueData
    C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.mapM P.N
      P.e P.hmapM P.hOpen P.thetaN P.hthetaN

end Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage

set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 400000 in
-- Selecting both finite families exposes many dependent quotient-algebra instances.
set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
/-- The simultaneous finite-stage descent producers inhabit the glue package. -/
theorem exists_pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k] :
    Nonempty (Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨L, n, m, relation, e, M, mapM, hmapM, hOpen, _⟩ :=
    exists_finSubext_pic0FiniteStageTransition_models (C := C) (F := F)
  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic L.1 k := by infer_instance
  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic M.1 k := by infer_instance
  let Q := pic0FiniteStageTripleModelComparisonFamily
    C L n m relation e M mapM hmapM
  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ :=
    exists_finSubext_pic0FiniteStageTripleTransition_models_of_comparisons
      C L n m relation M mapM Q
  choose thetaN hthetaN using hN
  exact ⟨{
    L := L
    n := n
    m := m
    relation := relation
    e := e
    M := M
    mapM := mapM
    hmapM := hmapM
    hOpen := hOpen
    N := N
    thetaN := thetaN
    hthetaN := by
      intro p
      simpa only [Q, pic0FiniteStageTransportedTripleTransitionOfModels] using
        hthetaN p
  }⟩

end

/-!

This module assembles the two projection equations for the right leg of the

separably closed atlas.

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

noncomputable section

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))

theorem gluingOverlapIso_pre_snd
    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F)
    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    ((Scheme.Pullback.gluing P.glueData.openCover P.gluedMap
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 k)))).t U V ≫
        (Scheme.Pullback.gluing P.glueData.openCover P.gluedMap
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 k)))).f V U) ≫
        (pullback.congrHom (glueData_ι_gluedMap C P V) rfl).hom =
      (gluingOverlapFlatteningIso C P U V).hom ≫
        (pullback.congrHom
          (glueData_f_comp_inclusion_comp_gluedMap C P U V) rfl).hom ≫
        rightRestrictionBaseChangeMap C P U V := by
  apply pullback.hom_ext
    (f := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
      (algebraMap P.N.1
        (Pic0FiniteStageChartBaseChangeRing
          C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N V))))
    (g := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 k)))
  · simpa only [Category.assoc] using
      gluingOverlapIso_pre_snd_fst C P U V
  · simpa only [Category.assoc] using
      gluingOverlapIso_pre_snd_snd C P U V

/-- The spectrum of the exact right restriction, followed by the right chart's
affine identification, is the affine-overlap identification. -/
theorem exactRightRestrictionAlgHom_fromSpec
    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
        (exactRightRestrictionAlgHom C U V).toRingHom) ≫
        V.1.2.fromSpec =
      (pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap C U V).2.fromSpec := by
  change Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
      (pic0FiniteStageRestrictionRight C U V).toRingHom) ≫
      V.1.2.fromSpec = _
  change Spec.map
      ((pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1.left.presheaf.map
        (homOfLE (pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap_le_right C U V)).op) ≫
      V.1.2.fromSpec = _
  exact V.1.2.map_fromSpec (pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap C U V).2
    (homOfLE (pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap_le_right C U V)).op

end Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0FiniteStageGluingOverlapIsoPreSnd

/-!
# The right leg of the finite-stage Picard gluing comparison

The overlap comparison in `Pic0FiniteStageGluingDiagramIso` respects the second
multispan leg as well as the first.  This is the remaining local naturality
equation needed to assemble the chart and overlap comparisons into a natural
isomorphism of gluing diagrams.

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits TensorProduct
open scoped TensorProduct

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

noncomputable section

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))

/-- The overlap comparison respects the right multispan projection. -/
theorem gluingOverlapIso_snd
    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F)
    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    ((Scheme.Pullback.gluing P.glueData.openCover P.gluedMap
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 k)))).t U V ≫
        (Scheme.Pullback.gluing P.glueData.openCover P.gluedMap
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 k)))).f V U) ≫
        (gluingChartIso C P V).hom =
      (gluingOverlapIso C P U V).hom ≫
        ((pic0SepClosedAtlasGlueData C).t U V ≫
          (pic0SepClosedAtlasGlueData C).f V U) := by
  have chart_fac :
      (chartBaseChangeIso C P V).hom ≫ V.1.1.ι =
        (chartRingBaseChangeIso C P V).hom ≫ V.1.2.fromSpec := by
    calc
      _ = (chartRingBaseChangeIso C P V).hom ≫
          (V.1.2.isoSpec.inv ≫ V.1.1.ι) := by
        simp only [chartBaseChangeIso, chartRingBaseChangeIso,
          chartFinalBaseChangeEquiv, affineBaseChangeIso, Iso.trans_hom,
          Iso.symm_hom, Category.assoc]
      _ = _ := congrArg (fun q => (chartRingBaseChangeIso C P V).hom ≫ q)
        V.1.2.isoSpec_inv_ι
  have overlap_fac :
      (overlapBaseChangeIso C P U V).hom ≫
          (pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap C U V).1.ι =
      (overlapRingBaseChangeIso C P U V).hom ≫
          (pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap C U V).2.fromSpec := by
    calc
      _ = (overlapRingBaseChangeIso C P U V).hom ≫
          ((pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap C U V).2.isoSpec.inv ≫
            (pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap C U V).1.ι) := by
        simp only [overlapBaseChangeIso, overlapRingBaseChangeIso,
          overlapFinalBaseChangeEquiv, affineBaseChangeIso, Iso.trans_hom,
          Iso.symm_hom, Category.assoc]
      _ = _ := congrArg

        (pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap C U V).2.isoSpec_inv_ι

    apply Multicoequalizer.hom_ext
    intro U

      (baseChangedGlueData C P).ι U ≫
          (gluingGluedHom C P ≫ gluingGluedInv C P) =
        ((gluingChartIso C P U).hom ≫
          (pic0SepClosedAtlasGlueData C).ι U) ≫
            gluingGluedInv C P := by
          rw [← Category.assoc, gluingGluedHom_ι C P U]

            (baseChangedGlueData C P).ι U) := by
        rw [Category.assoc, gluingGluedInv_ι C P U]
      _ = (baseChangedGlueData C P).ι U := by simp
      _ = (baseChangedGlueData C P).ι U ≫ 𝟙 _ := by simp

    apply Multicoequalizer.hom_ext
    intro U
    calc
      (pic0SepClosedAtlasGlueData C).ι U ≫
          (gluingGluedInv C P ≫ gluingGluedHom C P) =
        ((gluingChartIso C P U).inv ≫
          (baseChangedGlueData C P).ι U) ≫
            gluingGluedHom C P := by
          rw [← Category.assoc, gluingGluedInv_ι C P U]

        rw [Category.assoc, gluingGluedHom_ι C P U]
      _ = (pic0SepClosedAtlasGlueData C).ι U := by simp
      _ = (pic0SepClosedAtlasGlueData C).ι U ≫ 𝟙 _ := by simp
